set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-later; milestone-maintenance.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: At 8d4881a ContentLexicalSuite still claims agreement while SemanticDistance.lexicalJaccard delegates to the same scorer. Landed 4a8403ff contains that wording; minimal proof-description correction remains open.

Remaining / next action: Rename the lexical historical-provider comparison as a historical-adapter delegation regression guard; retain the six independent literal Jaccard expectations. Stronger historical parity requires an independent oracle.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

From Claude independent review of lexical bd-01M381YHAXMH9F5HZD8P7DKTBX at SHA a71a3ad9. ContentLexicalSuite test named typed lexical scoring agrees with historical provider now compares the typed scorer against its own Source shim, so it is a regression guard rather than an independent parity control. Rename or replace it to state its actual proof burden; retain the literal Jaccard grid, which killed L1 and L2. This is FOLLOW-UP, not a landing block, and should wait for the integrated slice to land.
